set_aside.subject: allocation amount precision during expense correction
set_aside.text: `AllocationInstruction.amount: Decimal` and `An amount's sign is not checked`, while A9 says stored monetary amounts are already exact to 2 fraction digits; `correct_expense` specifies validation of the total, sum and targets but no precision handling for individual allocations.
set_aside.question: When a correction contains allocation amounts with more than two fraction digits, must they be accepted unchanged, quantized before the sum check, or rejected?
options: Accept and store the exact Decimal values despite their extra fraction digits.
Quantize each allocation ROUND_HALF_UP to two digits, then check the sum and store it.
Reject any allocation amount that is not already exact to two fraction digits.
set_aside.default_guess: Quantize each allocation ROUND_HALF_UP to two digits before checking the sum and storing it.

witness.initial: An active project has an expense totaling EUR 10.00.
events: A staff operator corrects it with allocations of 3.333 and 6.667 to valid targets.
outcomes: The correction succeeds and stores 3.333 and 6.667 because individual amounts are unrestricted Decimals whose exact sum is 10.00.
The correction quantizes or rejects the allocations because persisted money must have exactly two fraction digits.
witness.observer: The operator sees success versus HTTP 422, or later readers see different stored allocation amounts.

set_aside.subject: deployment configurability of staff and viewer session lifetimes
set_aside.text: A30 calls staff and viewer session lifetimes runtime knobs whose deployment values may differ, but `create_runtime_app` says those values are fixed in use-case source and a deployment cannot change them.
set_aside.question: Must deployment-supplied session lifetime settings control issued session expiries, or are the source-code constants always used?
options: Use the values supplied through RuntimeSettings.
Ignore deployment values and always use the source-code constants.
set_aside.default_guess: Preserve the explicitly accepted running behavior and use the source-code constants.

witness.initial: A deployment supplies a staff session lifetime of one hour instead of the twelve-hour default.
events: The deployment creates the runtime application.
outcomes: The issued session expires after one hour because A30 defines the lifetime as a runtime knob.
The issued session expires after twelve hours because the use case uses its fixed source constant.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and signed-in staff member observe when the session stops authenticating.

set_aside.subject: transport-guard coverage of health routes
set_aside.text: `create_runtime_app` says the transport guard is installed before the inner application is mounted, but does not identify whether it is installed on the outer application or the inner application; A25 says every HTTP request passes it.
set_aside.question: Do `/health/live` and `/health/ready` pass through the transport guard, including trusted-host checks, headers and request logging?
options: Install the guard on the outer application so health and mounted API routes all pass through it.
Install the guard on the inner application so only mounted API routes pass through it and outer health routes bypass it.
set_aside.default_guess: Install the guard on the outer application so A25 applies to every request.

witness.initial: The service is running and configured to trust only `portal.example`.
events: A remote caller sends `GET /health/live` with an untrusted Host header.
outcomes: The outer transport guard refuses the request with 400.
The health route bypasses the inner application's guard and returns the normal successful health answer.
witness.observer: The remote health-check caller sees 400 versus success.
